# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the defusal manual, which states: "Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire, then the green wire."

I cannot see the bomb, so I do not know where these wires are located, how many wires exist, or their arrangement. Furthermore, I cannot speak and can only gesture to Deaf. Since gesture symbols carry no pre-established meaning for colors, sending gestures now would be ambiguous or misleading. 

Deaf can see the bomb and speak to the room, and Blind can feel the bomb and hear. The safest course is to wait for Deaf to inspect the bomb and speak to establish a code or layout so I can signal the correct wire sequence.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says: Tactile info for Mute: Keypad slots 1 to 4 are engraved with 8, 1, 5, 3. It requires 1 digit. Strip has 3 engraved symbols: first is a flower/rosette, second and third are identical trident/three-pronged fork shapes pointing down. There are 6 wire slots.
Deaf says: BOMB STATUS: DISPLAY is 0. LIGHT is green. STRIP is painted green, green, green. KEYPAD has 4 buttons: position 1 has 8, position 2 has 1, position 3 has 5, position 4 has 3. Needs 1 digit entered. WIRES (1 to 6): 1=purple, 2=white, 3=blue, 4=green, 5=red, 6=orange. Mute, check manual and gesture to me what Blind should do: use finger counts (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 4, 🖐=5, etc.). Gesture 👍 for cut wire, 👌 for press keypad. I will speak instructions to Blind.

Deaf has identified the wire colors and their positions: wire 1 is purple, wire 3 is blue, and wire 4 is green. Deaf also established the communication protocol: `👍` for cut wire, followed by finger counts for the wire index.

The manual instructs: "Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire, then the green wire."
The purple wire is wire 1. I will gesture to Deaf to cut wire 1 first.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: cut wire 1. Bomb update: DISPLAY is now 6, LIGHT is now blue. KEYPAD positions: 1 is 8, 2 is 1, 3 is 5, 4 is 3 (needs 1 digit, entered nothing). STRIP is green, green, green. Mute: gesture next action: 👍 + number (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖖=4, 🖐=5, 🤙=6) to cut wire; 👌 + position (☝=pos 1, ✌=pos 2, 🤟=pos 3, 🖖=pos 4) to press keypad button; 🙏 if defused or wait.

Wire 1 (purple) was successfully cut. Next in sequence from the manual is the blue wire, which Deaf identified as wire 3. Using Deaf's code (👍 for cut, 🤟 for 3), I will signal to cut wire 3.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤟"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Deaf says: Blind: cut wire 3. Bomb update: Wire 1 is CUT successfully. DISPLAY is now 9. LIGHT is blue. STRIP is green, green, green. KEYPAD: 1:[8], 2:[1], 3:[5], 4:[3] (needs 1 digit, entered nothing). WIRES: 1:CUT, 2:white, 3:blue, 4:green, 5:red, 6:orange. Mute: gesture next action (👍 + wire number to cut, 👌 + keypad position to press, or 🙏 if done).

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Deaf says: Blind: cut wire 4. Bomb update: Wire 3 is CUT. DISPLAY is 9, LIGHT is blue. KEYPAD: 1:[8], 2:[1], 3:[5], 4:[3] (needs 1 digit). Remaining uncut WIRES: 2:white, 4:green, 5:red, 6:orange. Mute: gesture next action (👍 + number to cut, 👌 + keypad position to press, 🙏 if done).

Wire 4 (green) is the final wire specified in the defusal manual ("Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire, then the green wire"). Blind is about to cut wire 4 based on Deaf's instruction from last round.

Since there are no further steps in the manual, I will gesture `🙏` to signal to Deaf that defusal will be complete and no further actions are required.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏"])
```
